Dr. M McLaren
Neurologist
Suite 3
67 The Crescent
Newtown

09/08/14

Dear Dr. McLaren,
Re: Mr. Michael Weir, DOB: 20/09/1970

I am writing this letter to refer Mr. Weir, a 43-year-old married man, whose features are
suggestive of multiple sclerosis.

Mr. Weir is a smoker and has had depression since September 2012, for which he takes Zoloft.

On 26/06/14, the patient attended my clinic complaining of fatigue and stress. His examination
was unremarkable except for a BP of 96/83 and high BMI (27.8). Therefore, CBC and lipid
tests were ordered. After one week, he reported having weakness in his left leg. Test results
showed decreased levels of WBC, RBC, Hb and Hct, whereas his cholesterol level was 6.37
mmol/L; thus, the patient was advised to decrease saturated fat intake and to exercise in order to
lose weight.

Unfortunately, today he presented with dizziness and two recent blackouts as well as a tingling
sensation in his hands. His examination revealed a loss of sensation on both hands plus a
diminished left patellar reflex. As a result, CTs of the head and lumbar spine were ordered,
however, an MRI might also be needed.

In view of the above, I am referring this patient for your further neurological assessment. Please
do not hesitate to contact me

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
